articleTitle: Automated FISH Signals Fusion Detection for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Cancer is considered as one of the undefeatable diseases around the world that occur due to the uncontrollable growth of abnormal cells [1]. In 2012, according to World Health Organization (WHO) and Cancer Research UK, 14.1 million adults in the world have been diagnosed by cancer, 58% of them died of it [2]. In Egypt and according to its national cancer registry institute, 108,600 have been diagnosed by cancer 66% of them died. Leukemia is cancer of the body's blood-forming tissues, including the bone marrow and the lymphatic system. Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) is a type of blood cancer that causes the body to produce a large number of white blood cells. In 2012 according to WHO, 352,000 have been diagnosed with leukemia, 75% of them died of it. In 2013, 1125 diagnosed with Myeloid leukemia in Egypt [3]. In this research, FISH (Florescent In Situ Hybridization) images is the key factor of detecting abnormalities in genes. CML can be detected using FISH. CML diagnosis depends on the detection of fused red and green signals. Our approach first detects signals, their colors, and then fusion between these colors. Moreover, number of fusions need to be counted in order to specify the treatment. Our system achieved an accuracy of 98% which proofs the efficiency of the approach.

articleTitle: Chaotic Based Technique for Partial Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Selective or partial encryption of images can greatly reduce the computational complexity and execution time by encoding just a small amount of the image pixels. The selected image pixels correspond to the image region of interest. In this paper, a Chaotic and Cipher based technique for selective encryption of images is introduced. In this technique, the low correlated pseudo random number sequences, the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), and Arnold Cat Map (ACM) permutation techniques are utilized. For a given image, the rows and columns of the image are summed individually to form two vectors named vertical and horizontal vectors respectively. Then, the subsequent vertical and horizontal vectors are summed once more to form the overall summation vector which reflects the amount of information distribution within the image. The mean of the summation vector is calculated. The intersection of mean line and the summation curve builds up different regions above and beneath the mean line. The areas of these regions are computed separately. The largest area is taken as the sensitive area. The simulation results indicate that the proposed technique is less time consuming and more robust than the traditional full image encryption techniques.

articleTitle: Hybrid Techniques for Fast and Low Complexity MIMO Detection
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Sphere Decoding (SD) can minimize the complexity of Maximum Likelihood Decoding (MLD) without loss of performance, but its complexity and execution time are still high for applying it into practical Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems. In this paper, a new technique for MIMO signal detection using a hybrid combination between SD and linear detectors is proposed. The proposed technique is intended to reduce the complexity and execution time of the detection process. The main idea is based on splitting the vector of transmitted symbols and the channel matrix into two equal size subsets, where the received symbols detection process will be performed in two separate successive stages. It is proposed to use the SD for the first stage for accurate estimation of the first subset of symbols, which has a critical influence on the next stage performance. Low complexity detectors such as Zero Forcing (ZF) and Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) are utilized to estimate the second subset of symbols in order to reduce the complexity. In this case, the SD search in the whole lattice is avoided. Only a half search burden is required which will lead to a significant saving in the computational complexity and time.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulations by Parallelization of the Linear Equation Solver Using Wavefront Technique
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) uses numerical analysis methods and algorithms to solve and analyze problems that involve fluid flows. These algorithms require very high computational power that does not exist in traditional computers systems. This paper presents code accelerated methodology by parallelizing the linear equation solver and is developed to provide the numerical solution of the steady Navier-Stokes equations, using the Finite Volume Method (FVM) in primitive variables formulation. A case study of incompressible flow in a 2D lid-driven square cavity is investigated for Re=1000. Detailed second order spatially accurate results, where the tertiary vortices were observed, are presented. Co-located grid arrangements along with a uniform structured Cartesian grid up to 701*701 were used. Strongly implicit procedure is used to solve the resulted linear algebraic equations. The parallelization of SIP solver is implemented by using wave-front technique and was implemented using OpenMP with multi-core processor. The solution time was reduced by 26%.

articleTitle: Discriminative EdgeBoxes for Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Due to the huge amount of online videos uploaded and viewed every day, there is an emerging need nowadays for action recognition techniques. These techniques need to consider the large variations in camera motion, viewpoint, cluttered background, etc. Moreover, they need to be unsupervised or weakly supervised to can absorb such amount of different actions. The goal of this paper is to introduce a new unsupervised technique for mining mid-level discriminative patches from videos. These patches are the most representative parts that can describe an action. To achieve this goal, we generalize a technique borrowed from 2D images to generate bounding boxes with high motion and appearance saliencies then apply iterative clustering/classification procedure on generated boxes. Then, we calculate discriminative score for each box and finally select top ranked boxes to train Exemplar-SVM on low-level features extracted inside selected boxes. We evaluate our approach on a challenging dataset namely YouTube and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach to achieve better average recognition accuracy than the state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: An Optimization Strategy for Improving Security in Steganography
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: To improve the security performance of steganography, many adaptive steganographic algorithms have been presented recently. These algorithms enhance the security mainly by pixel-level's adaption while paying no attention to the image-level's adaption. Image-level's adaption means that different images have different characteristics and thus should be considered with different steganographic strategy. In this paper, we propose an optimization strategy to achieve image-level's adaption based on the texture. In the proposed method, we treat different images with individual steganography strategy according to their textures. For each cover image, a bank of Wavelet filters is assessed and the one to achieve the smallest change of the image, with respect of features used in steganalyzer, after embedding the message is adopted. The experiment result shows that the proposed method improves the security significantly compared with the state-of-arts adaptive steganographic algorithms.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Fractal Shape For S-Band,C-Band & Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: A novel technique for miniaturization of microstrip patch antenna is proposed for Portable and multifunctional Communication systems. Our proposed design consists of fractal patch, E-Shaped slot on fractal patch with first iteration and combination of H-Shape and L-Shape slots on the Ground plane. In this way we get smaller size antenna which is smaller than the conventional antenna. The most interesting feature of our proposed design is that we are getting multiband response in the frequency range of 1-8GHZ having Directivity in the range of 3.58dBi-6.39dBi, Gain in the range of 2.43dB-5.32dB and good impedance bandwidth for desired bands. As we have used the fractal patch with substrate FR4. Co-axial cable is used as a feeding method. We also employed shorting pin between fractal patch and ground plane. By the combination of all these proposed technique size of antenna is reduced 60.60% and it produces multiband response while the impedance bandwidth and gain are satisfactory for each band. We can adjust different bands by changing position of shorting pin. This type of smaller size antenna has applications in mobile phone as well as for S-Band and C-Band applications.

articleTitle: High Impact Bugs Recommender Model
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Software systems grow quickly in size and become very complicated to maintain. There are many activities that are required to manage software systems including maintenance related activities such as handling software bugs. Modern software management techniques mandate efficient scheduling of the executed tasks. Thus, the project manager needs to triage software bugs accurately. To achieve deeper understanding of bugs, we must classify bugs into modern classification categories. In this paper, we will focus on the recognition of high impact bugs. We aim to automate the classification process instead of the manual approach. We will study four thousand issue reports in four open source projects (Ambari, Camel, Derby and Wicket). We suggest making automatic classification in two layers. The first layer is divided into two categories: low-impact bugs and high impact bugs. The second layer classifies high impact bugs into: surprise, dormant, blocking, security, performance, and breakage bug types. The main aim of this research is to help the system maintenance engineer by providing a recommender model that can help him with future error reports. For newly reported bugs, it will give him prediction of high impact ones and their type.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a New Hybrid Defense Mechanism Against DDoS Attacks
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: DDoS attacks leads cybercrime attacks and considered as the most difficult type of attacks because attackers use fake identities and launched using IP spoofing and deceive target servers by masquerading legitimate identity. Some of the existing techniques (e.g., Traceback and Hop Count) focus on tracking the source of the attack and identify malicious packets during the attack. This paper proposed a new hybrid defense mechanism that filters the traffic of packets at early stage before reaching target server and blocks malicious packets. A set of experiments were carried out using OPNET Modeler network simulation software showing that the accuracy of the proposed mechanism is 99.97%.

articleTitle: Neural Network Approach for Modeling of Low-Cost Inertial Navigation System Errors
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: The nonlinear autoregressive with exogenous input (NARX) network is a dynamical neural architecture commonly used for input-output modeling of dynamical systems. Micro-electro-mechanical-system (MEMS)-based inertial navigation system (INS) was integrated with GPS to achieve more robust positioning and orientation information. In many GPS/INS integration schemes, the linear errors of MEMS-based INS were estimated precisely while the higher order errors were ignored. This paper presents a new method to model nonlinear errors of MEMS INS by using NARX algorithm. The NARX algorithm was augmented with common Kalman filter (KF) linear predictor to enhance the overall system performance. The NARX technique has been proven to predict MEMS-based gyro nonlinear errors during GPS outage with an acceptable accuracy. Results obtained from the proposed augmented KF/NARX technique show a better root mean square (MSE) positional and azimuth errors.

articleTitle: Forecasting Rainfall Based On Hybrid Intelligent System
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Forecasting the weather in future won the attention of many researchers in different countries around the world. In this work a robust hybrid technique was applied to forecast rainfall by combining Particle Swarm Optimization based Learning Automata (PSOLA) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) which is popular kind used in Feed Forward Neural Network (FFNN). The proposed technique solves the flaw of PSO through implementing it in two steps, first step construct ANN - MLP and second step generate optimal weights by (PSOLA) based on four weather parameters. These parameters are Minimum temperature (Min temperature), Maximum temperature (Max temperature), Humidity, and Wind Speed as input parameters whereas rain rate parameter considered as output. Trained MLP to predict rainfall based on weights driven from the second phase. The simulation result of the hybrid technique represents that Mean Square Error (MSE) of testing dataset is 0.9.

articleTitle: Advanced Neural Network Gait Recognition System with Dynamic Thresholding
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Non-interactive biometric systems have gained an enormous interest among computer vision researchers as they provide more efficient and reliable ways of identification and verification from distance. Face and gait recognition are types of non-interactive biometric systems as they do not need user cooperation with the surveillance system. Gait recognition is more efficient than face recognition as it can deal with low resolution and brightness images. Gait recognition aims to recognize people based on the way they walk. In this paper, we propose a surveillance system for human identification using a neural network with an enhanced back-propagation algorithm. This neural network is fed with time-varying 1D distance signals calculated from an extracted silhouette sequence. Initially, background modeling is performed for the video sequence. Subsequently, the moving object is being segmented using background subtraction with dynamic thresholding. Then, the neural network is trained with the extracted distance signals. Finally, when the target image sequence is fed, the proposed system extracts features and the identification is performed with the classifier. The proposed system is evaluated using a gait database and it achieves a good recognition performance.

articleTitle: An Intelligent XML Information Retrieval System
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: eXtensible Markup Language (XML) is widely used due to the characteristics of self-describing, scalable, and flexibility for representing different types of information in a single unified way. Information retrieval systems (IR) have become essential in finding relevant information within XML data. The growing volume of XML contents in many domains has motivated the research on how to retrieve XML data efficiently and effectively. XML information retrieval (XML-IR) systems main process is searching XML document fragments relevant to queries from a collection of XML documents. This paper aims at integrating IR and XML search techniques that could enable more sophisticated search on the structure as well as the content of the documents. This paper proposes an intelligent method of ranking XML documents with respect to an IR query by means of fuzzy logic. The proposed system deals with vague, uncertainty, and imprecise queries that allow it to be evaluated against an XML document collection. Experimental results show good performance of the proposed system compared to ADXPI system.

articleTitle: Light Weight Encryption for Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In medical images such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), a lot of image information is created. Such images need a huge storage disk space and large bandwidth to be transmitted over the network. So, efficient storage and transmission technique is urgent to reduce the required storage capacity and transmission bandwidth. In this paper, an effective and low complexity transmission technique of medical images is proposed. Owing to the fact that in medical images, only a little partition of the image may be diagnostically useful, the medical image contents can be classified into two main parts; one for the region of interest (ROI) and the other for the non-region of interest (NON-ROI). The image containing the ROI is lossless compressed to save the important diagnostically details, while the image containing the remaining part (NON-ROI) is lossy compressed. The lossless compression allows the ROI reconstruction without losing any details. In addition to storage and bandwidth saving, the general compression techniques achieve an attractive level of security that permits secure transmission of the image in the restricted bandwidth over the network. Furthermore, to increase privacy and protect the important data from non-authorized access the region of interest is encrypted using strong encryption technique such as Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) technique. The encrypted ROI is lossless compressed before transmission after AES encryption process. The decompressed images are fused to reconstruct the entire image, at the receiving end.

articleTitle: A Repaired Genetic Algorithm Based Approach for Web Service Security Negotiation
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In the field of Service Oriented Architecture (SOA), managing the non-functional requirements of SOA security is an important trend. This is due to the different levels of security the consumer and the provider demand or supply. A web service may have different implementations having the same functionality, but may have different security constraints. Thus, finding a service support a security level that is acceptable to all parties is the main problem. So, automated negotiation among services is conducted to get an acceptable security level or a solution for all sides. This paper proposes a Repaired Genetic Security Service based negotiation approach for finding an acceptable security level in the multi-lateral multi-objective environment. With the evaluation of that approach, proposed approach outperforms the traditional time-based negotiation strategy. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of the genetic algorithm used in the web service security negotiation problem.

articleTitle: Improving Performance of TCP variants in Long Term Evolution (LTE)
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: In recent years, Long Term Evolution (LTE) networks are quickly deployed everywhere in the world to resolve the congestion problem in 3G networks. Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides reliable delivery of data stream at the transport layer. Several TCP variants have been proposed. They can be used to enhance quality of service (QoS). In this paper, an enhanced approach is proposed to improve the performance congestion control in LTE network. The proposed approach depends on controlling the receive buffer size in eNode B. This will be performed through dividing the memory size of eNode B between active users. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach that leads to enhance performance in terms of network throughput and low time delay.

articleTitle: Event-driven Modeling Test Case Generation with Holistic View for Multilevel Services Composition
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: A service-oriented architecture for web applications is often implemented using web services. These services can be combined in a new workflow called as web service composition. These services have become more and more complex, where they have to cope with strict requirements of business processes and their dynamic evolution, and interactions among different companies. In this context, the analysis and testing of such services demands a large amount of effort. To reduce the effort required for web-services testing, in this paper, we propose an event-driven approach to automatically modeling and generating test cases that enable a comfortable fault management leading to a holistic view for multilevel web services composition. To evaluate our approach, we applied it to four cases study using our developed tool. Compared to exiting approaches, our approach reduces testing cost and execution time, and increases testing reliability.

articleTitle: Low Dose CT Image Restoration by Incremental Learning and Ant Colony Optimization
publicationTitle: 2016 26th International Conference on Computer Theory and Applications (ICCTA)
abstract: Patch priors play a key issue in patch based image restoration tasks. The main idea is to learn a good and adaptive image prior over small image patches. However, expected patch log ikelihood (EPLL) framework achieved a good performance in image restoration applications, it mainly employs the Gaussian Mixture model (GMM) prior over a large number of training patches which gains a huge computational cost. On the other hand, the GMM parameters are learned with the Expectation Maximization (EM) algorithm which usually suffers from local optimum problem. This paper proposes a post filter by extending the EPLL framework to reduce noise in CT images acquired on low radiation dose, in order to get a better quality image with fine details preserved. The basic idea is to incrementally estimate the mixture component parameters to skip over the significant drawback of the (EM) algorithm which greatly depends on the initialization of model parameters. Incremental method with split-merge mixtures learning (SMILE) is utilized for learning mixture models by consecutive split and merge operations. Then, the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm is used to select homogeneous patches which tend to cluster together due to the local spatial smoothness in the image. Instead of restoring each patch separately, the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation is employed to denoise the homogeneous patches selected by ACO algorithm. The proposed method leads to better clustering results and superior denoised results.
